title: Effects and Evidence Synthesis of the Use of  Complementary and Alternative Medicine in Adults Undergoing Chemotherapy Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
content: Chemotherapy is essential in the treatment of cancer, but its adverse effects affect quality of life and pharmacological therapy is insufficient to control it. Evidence of non-pharmacological interventions is limited and heterogeneous, requiring rigorous syn-theses. Objective: To systematically review the effect of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) in managing side effects in adults with cancer undergoing chemothera-py. Methods: Following JBI and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS for clinical trials (2015–2025) evaluating bio-based, mind-body, and energy therapies in cancer patients aged 20–74. Quantitative data were meta-analyzed using DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models in Review Manager to calculate Hedges' g. Results: Of 1109 identified studies, 42 met the inclusion criteria and 26 provided data for meta-analysis. CAM significantly improved sleep quality (8 studies, n = 712, g = 1.008, p = 0.0002, I²: 90.9%) and cancer-related fatigue (9 studies, n = 752, g = 0.659, p < 0.0001, I²=72.7%), and significantly reduced nausea/vomiting (13 studies, n = 989, g = 2.099, p < 0.0001, I²=97.7%,). Sensitivity analyses confirmed these findings were stable and robust against high-risk-of-bias studies. Conclusions: The findings suggest the studies are predominantly in Asian populations and in people with breast cancer and the use of CAM shows a potential benefit as an adjunct intervention to conventional treat-ment in reducing secondary symptoms of chemotherapy, although the marked heteroge-neity suggests caution in their interpretation. Greater standardization of intervention protocols is required to strengthen the certainty of evidence in oncology nursing practice.
